sentences.text: Heard learned advocate Mr. Jaydev Bhatt for learned advocate Mr. Hriday Buch for the appellant and learned Assistant Government Pleader Mr. Rahul Dave for respondent No.1.

The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1.
On 04.03.2016, appellant visited the place of opponent Nos.2 to 6 with a Panch witness.
In presence of opponent No.2, appellant found 15 kg packed tin of Groundnut oil of Gayatri Brand and about 10 tins were stored for retail sale.
The samples which were received by appellant, were sent to Food Safety Officer in sealed cover.

On 21.03.2016, the report of the Food Analyst found that the sample of Gayatri Singtel manufacturing month February 2016, B.No.4 is misbranded under Regulation No.2.2.1.2 of Food Safety and Standard (Packaging and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined Labelling)
Regulations, 2011 and the provisions of the said Act, and Rules made thereunder in respect of the name of food in Gujarati language only.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the Adjudicating Officer vide order dated 04.03.2017 found the manufacturers as well as the retailers guilty of the offence punishable under Section 52 of the said Act and imposed penalty of Rs.3,000/- each to the opponent Nos.2 to 6 and Rs.6,000/- each to the manufacturers of the Gayatri Brand Coconut oil namely original-opponent Nos.6 to 10.
The manufacturers accepted order of the Adjudicating Officer and paid the penalty imposed upon them.

However, present respondent Nos.2 to 6 being the retailers challenged the order of imposing penalty by way of an Appeal before learned Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Gujarat State at Gandhinagar being First Appeal No.67 of 2017, wherein learned Presiding Officer set aside the order of imposing penalty and acquitted respondent Nos.1 to 5 under the Adjudication Application No.5 of 2017 on 01.03.2019.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned order, the appellant has preferred this Appeal.

4. Learned advocate for the appellant, at the outset, submitted that the order impugned is bad in law and exoneration of opponent Nos.2 to 6 is nothing but an overlooking of the provisions of Section 26 (2) (ii) and Section 27 (2) (c) of the said Act.
It is contended that learned Appellate Tribunal has committed an error by resorting to Section 80(B) (2) (d) (i) of the said Act.

It is further contended that no defence is available to respondent Nos.2 to 6 herein in the cases where an offence pertaining to the sale of any unsafe or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the food business operator was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of the food sold by him or that the purchaser having purchased any article for analysis was not prejudiced by the sale.

It is further contended that before the Adjudicating Authority, the defence of due diligence was never raised and the statement dated 22.02.2017 was given by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined opponents stating that sample has been declared as misbranded and opponents will be careful in future with regard to compliance of provisions of the said Act and Regulations made thereunder.

sentences.text: Adjudicating Authority, such defence of due diligence is not available to respondent Nos.2 to 6 before the learned Appellate Tribunal.
Learned Appellate Tribunal has wrongly applied provisions of Section 80 (B) (2) (d) (i) of the said Act.

5. Per contra, learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 has contended that learned Appellant Tribunal has rightly applied the provisions of Section 80 (B) (2) (d) (i) of the said Act and acquitted respondent Nos.2 to 6, and rightly quashed and set aside the order of penalty.
It is further contended that the reliance placed upon by the appellant on Sub- section (E) (iv) of Section 80 is not applicable.

Sub-section (E) of Section 80 would be applicable in the cases where the issue is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined with regard to nature, substance or quality of food and in those facts and circumstances, no defence is available in a prosecution for an offence pertaining to the sale of any unsafe or misbranded article of food.

In the present case, it is an admitted fact that the sample was purchased by the appellant from respondent Nos.2 to 6 in a sealed package and the respondent Nos.2 to 6 were selling product under the same condition.
The due diligence defence is available to the respondent Nos.2 to 6 and therefore, in absence of any contrary material, the appeal is required to be dismissed.
6. I have heard the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for the parties and perused the Paper-book.

Undisputedly, the report of the Food Analyst dated 21.03.2016 indicates that the sample of Gayatri Singtel in 15 kg manufacturing month February 2016, B.No.4 was purchased by Officer of Appellant from respondent Nos.2 to 6 who are retailers of the said product.

The product was declared as NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined misbranded under Regulation No.2.2.1.2 of Food Safety and Standard (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 and the provisions of the said Act, and Rules made thereunder in respect of the name of food in Gujarati language only.

sentences.text: The Adjudicating Authority after considering the statements given by respondents as well as partners of manufacturers imposed a penalty of Rs.3,000/- each on respondent Nos.2 to 6 and Rs.6,000/- each on the manufacturers of the product namely Gayatri Singtel.
The Appellate Tribunal disturbed the order of imposition of penalty upon respondent Nos.2 to 6 on an appeal filed by respondent Nos.2 to 6.

On perusal of the memo of appeal filed by respondent Nos.2 to 6, it appears that the contention which is raised in the appeal is that for the quality of goods, the offence is committed by Gayatri Industries and its partners.
The product was purchased by respondent Nos.2 to 6 from Gayatri Industries and its partners for sale and the packed material was taken by the Food Safety Officer from respondent Nos.2 to 6.

If the order of the Adjudicating Authority is considered who observed that NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined the original opponents gave a statement on 22.02.2017 that the sample has been declared as a misbranded and samples have never failed in past.
However, in future, necessary care shall be taken.

Before the learned Adjudicating Authority, respondent Nos.2 to 6, it appears that no defence of due diligence was raised and the defence of due diligence has been raised for the first time before learned Tribunal.

However, if the provisions of Section 80 of the said Act are perused, it explicitly mandates that there shall not be defence in a prosecution for an offence pertaining to the sale of any unsafe or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the food business operator was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of the food sold by him or that the purchaser having purchased any article for analysis was not prejudiced by the sale.

7. Resultantly, First Appeal is allowed.
The judgment and order dated 01.03.2019 passed by learned Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Gujarat State, Gandhinagar in First Appeal No.67 of 2017 is hereby quashed and set aside.
